changelog:
**A YouTube playlist can be added to a channel again.** Pasting a link into the Content list put a row on it, and then Save answered **HTTP 400** and nothing was written - not the link and not any other change to that channel. The page wrote the link's source with an empty id where the server wants a real one; the server could not read the body at all, so it refused the whole channel before any of it was looked at. Links carry the empty id properly now, and adding one, saving, and reading it back is checked against a real server before every release.

**A selected row can be let go of.** Selecting a row in the Content list is what arms the keyboard - Delete removes it, Alt with an arrow moves it - and the only ways to un-select were clicking that exact row again or finding the thin strip of list below the last one. Clicking anywhere else on the page left the row marked selected with the keyboard nowhere near it. Turning your attention elsewhere now lets it go: a click anywhere outside the list, or tabbing out of it. Escape still does it too, and the bar's own Move and Remove buttons do not count as leaving.

**Series come before episodes in search.** Films, series, collections and episodes were asked for in one request, so the server decided the order and put episodes wherever relevance landed them - a series' own episodes above the series itself, and for a long-running show, twenty episodes and no series row at all. The two are asked for separately now: titles first, in the server's own order, and the episodes after them.

**The channel-list preview's words fit the row again.** The row was given the television's real proportions last release - 78dp tall with the banner beside it - which makes it a sliver about thirty pixels high, and the four lines of text inside it kept the sizes they had when it was three times taller. They ran over each other. Everything in the row is now a share of its height, taken from the app: the name, what is on, the progress bar and what is next, all at the app's own sizes.
description: Lightweight virtual TV channels: deterministic schedules over your own library, tuned in via normal direct playback at the live position. No transcoding, no tuner emulation.
name: LiteTV Channels
overview: TV channels from your library, without transcoding.
